people.name: Neil D. McKay

website.source_note: Personal homepage (U-M EECS), already on record; resolves

people.current_position: Staff Research Engineer, General Motors Research (retired per record)

bio.summary: Neil D. McKay earned a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from the University of Michigan in 1985 under Kang G. Shin, with a thesis on minimum-cost control of robotic manipulators. McKay then joined General Motors Research labs as a Staff Research Engineer, working on mobile robot control, robot manipulator calibration, computer vision calibration and computer graphics. McKay taught computer graphics at the University of Michigan in Fall 1996.
research_areas: Robot manipulator control and trajectory planning
bio.thesis_title: Minimum-Cost Control of Robotic Manipulators with Geometric Path Constraints

people.name: Ming-Syan (Frank) Chen

website.source_note: Personal homepage at NTU NetDB Lab

people.current_position: Distinguished Professor of Electrical Engineering and NTU Chair Professor, National Taiwan University

bio.summary: Ming-Syan Chen received the M.S. (1985) and Ph.D. (1988) in Computer, Information and Control Engineering from the University of Michigan. Chen was a research staff member at IBM T. J. Watson Research Center (1988-1996), President/CEO of the Institute for Information Industry (2007-2008), and Distinguished Research Fellow at Academia Sinica (2008-2015). Chen is a Distinguished Professor and NTU Chair Professor at National Taiwan University and served as Dean of the College of EECS (2015-2018) and Executive Vice President (2019-2023).

people.name: Jyh-Charn (Steve) Liu
people.current_position: Professor Emeritus, Computer Science & Engineering, Texas A&M University

bio.summary: Jyh-Charn (Steve) Liu received the Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the University of Michigan in 1989, after B.S. and M.S. degrees from National Cheng Kung University. Liu joined Texas A&M University in 1989 as assistant professor and is now Professor Emeritus of Computer Science and Engineering. Liu directed the Real Time Distributed Systems Lab, working on real-time distributed computing, cyber-physical systems security and behavior modeling.

people.name: Parameswaran Ramanathan
people.current_position: Professor and Vilas Distinguished Achievement Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Wisconsin-Madison

bio.summary: Parameswaran (Parmesh) Ramanathan received the Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering from the University of Michigan in 1989, after an M.S.E. (1986) there and a B.Tech. from IIT Bombay (1984). Ramanathan joined UW-Madison in 1989 and chaired the ECE department from 2005 to 2009. Research spans ultrafast networks, millimeter-wave wireless sensing, smart grid technology and genomic networks.
